claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Since he's 17, I need to ask a couple more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training? If so, could you tell me what type of course or training he's enrolled in?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college counts as qualifying full-time education.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning you live with him and pay for things like food, clothing, and other expenses for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I pay for everything - his food, clothes, school supplies, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more question: Are you currently living in the UK? And could you also confirm whether you have British or Irish citizenship, or have the right to access public funds in the UK (for example, through settled status or another immigration status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- You are a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is 17 years old and lives with you
- You are responsible for him (paying for food, clothes, school supplies, etc.)
- He is in full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **You meet the residency requirement** – You're a British citizen living in the UK.

✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – He lives with you and you pay for his food, clothes, and other expenses.

✅ **Alex qualifies despite being over 16** – Although the standard eligibility is for children under 16, Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved full-time education.

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as he stays in approved education or training, until he turns 20 (whichever comes first).

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
